parts:
Hello unmarked friends,

Question about violations of the assumptions of the dynamic occupancy model


Goal of my study: estimate temporal effects and survey length effects on the detection probability of occupied nests of Chimney Swift. We want to know this to inform protocols to effectively detect occupied chimneys...


Methods: We recorded the presence (1)/absence (0) of Chimney Swifts entering or exiting nest sites every 10 min within a 60 survey. So encounter histories look like ... 001011 for example. We repeated this survey at 47 nests 3 to four times over the nesting season. So this is a dynamic occupancy design but with only one year.


I have gone ahead with a colext model, but became concerned that the sampling occasions are NOT independent, which would be a violation of an assumption for dynamic occupancy models (Kéry 2012 colext vignette; pg. 3). So the real question is “are the 10-min intervals within a 60-min survey independent?” Within a survey, the encounter histories average 1.3 detections. This is due to the relatively long foraging bouts between nest visits, but mean detections across all intervals are constant (~0.3)... so... are the 10-min intervals independent? If not, would a better route be to conform my data to fit a removal occupancy model (i.e., NAs after the first detection)?


Many thanks to this wonderful group!

Myles
